check.py.content_utf8:
from klippy.gcode import GCodeDispatch
from threading import Lock
from klippy.extras.display_status import DisplayStatus
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

class Host:
    def __init__(self):
        self.options={"debuginput":False}
        self.reactor=SimpleNamespace(mutex=Lock)
        self.dispatch=GCodeDispatch(self)
        self.display=DisplayStatus(self)
    def get_printer(self): return self
    def get_reactor(self): return self.reactor
    def get_start_args(self): return self.options
    def register_event_handler(self,event,fn): pass
    def lookup_object(self,name,default=None):
        if name=="gcode": return self.dispatch
        if name=="print_stats": return SimpleNamespace(get_status=lambda t:{"state":"standby"})
        return default
    def command_error(self,text):
        return RuntimeError(text)
    def send_event(self,name,*args): pass

h=Host()
h.dispatch._handle_ready()
script=Path("hello.gcode").read_text()
h.dispatch.run_script(script)
state=h.display.get_status(0.0)
assert state["message"]=="Hello, World!",state
print(state["message"])

semantic_scope: Klipper’s actual G-code dispatcher invoked the M117 display command from the original file. Its display-status module stored the exact message in a fixture without a printer or motion.
